entities.summary: Jérôme-Joseph de Momigny was a prominent Belgian/French composer and music-theorist of the Early Modern era. Born on January 20, 1762, in Philippeville, Hainaut, Belgium, he spent his early years studying music in Paris before transitioning to a career in music theory. De Momigny's compositions were heavily influenced by the Classical and Romantic periods, and he was particularly known for his work on the piano and orchestral works. His treatise on the piano, 'Traité élémentaire de la musique,' published in 1813, was a seminal work in the development of piano music during this period. De Momigny's legacy can be seen in the works of later composers, such as Chopin and Liszt, who built upon his theories and compositions. De Momigny's contributions to the development of piano music and his influence on later composers make him a significant figure in the history of music, particularly in the context of the Early Modern era. His compositions, though not as widely known today, remain an important part of music history, demonstrating the significance of his work in shaping the course of piano music.
